quotes.text: Azure Arc is not a cloud. It doesn't replace your data center. It doesn't migrate your servers anywhere. Think of it as a bridge.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up the most common misconception about Azure Arc.

quotes.text: You don't need to migrate anything to get Azure's management capabilities. You don't move your workloads. You don't re-architect your applications. You just connect what you already have to Azure's management plane.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core idea of Arc in plain terms.

quotes.text: Here's the best part. The agent is free. Connecting a server to Azure Arc costs nothing. You only pay for the services you enable on top
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies the cost model of Arc.

quotes.text: You stop thinking about my Azure servers and my AWS servers and start thinking about simply my servers. The location becomes a property of the resource, not a separate management domain.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable framing of unified multi-cloud management.

quotes.text: Here's the thing, the real value of Azure Arc isn't any single feature. It's integration, not the agent, not the policies, not the monitoring.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up why Arc matters as a whole.

chapters.title: What Arc is not and getting started

takeaways: Azure Arc is not a cloud and moves nothing; it projects servers, Kubernetes clusters and SQL Server instances outside Azure into Azure Resource Manager.

The free Connected Machine agent connects outbound over HTTPS, so Azure Policy, RBAC, tags, Defender for Cloud, Sentinel, Azure Monitor and Update Manager work the same on-premises, in AWS and in GCP.
Start small: register the resource providers, onboard one test server with the generated script, then add policy, Defender and update management step by step.
hook: Servers spread across your data center, Azure, AWS and Google Cloud, each with its own console? This episode explains Azure Arc in plain English for IT admins managing hybrid and multi-cloud estates, showing how one control plane brings governance, security, monitoring and patching to every server.
